name: MHC Class Ib Deficiency

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: MHC Class Ib Deficiency Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Identification of pathogenic mutations in genes encoding MHC Class Ib molecules (e.g., HLA-E, HLA-F, HLA-G)
Reduced or absent expression of MHC Class Ib molecules on peripheral blood mononuclear cells
Recurrent severe infections and evidence of immune dysregulation (autoimmunity or inflammatory manifestations)
Exclusion of classical MHC Class Ia deficiencies and other primary immunodeficiencies

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of pathogenic mutations in MHC Class Ib genes plus clinical presentation of recurrent infections and immune dysregulation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires integration of genetic, immunophenotypic, and clinical data.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Absent or markedly reduced MHC Class Ib molecule expression
pathognomonic.notes: Detected by flow cytometry or immunohistochemistry
searchTerms: absent or low MHC class Ib molecules
lack of MHC class Ib on cells

pathognomonic.symptomName: Severe recurrent bacterial and viral infections
pathognomonic.notes: Particularly affecting respiratory and gastrointestinal tracts
searchTerms: frequent serious bacterial and viral infections
repeated infections from bacteria and viruses
autoimmune problems due to immune imbalance

common.notes: Persistent fungal infections of skin and mucosa
searchTerms: chronic yeast infections on skin and mucous

common.symptomName: Failure to thrive in pediatric patients
common.notes: Due to chronic infections and inflammation
searchTerms: failure to gain weight and grow
increased markers of inflammation in blood
immune system destroying red blood cells
red blood cell breakdown from antibodies

occasional.notes: Secondary to infections or immune dysregulation

rare.symptomName: Severe anaphylactic reactions to blood transfusions
searchTerms: severe allergic reactions to blood transfusions

laboratory: Flow cytometry showing absent or reduced MHC Class Ib molecule expression
imaging: Chest CT showing interstitial lung disease
Lymph node enlargement on ultrasound or CT
genetic: Pathogenic variants in HLA-E, HLA-F, or HLA-G genes
Possible compound heterozygous or homozygous mutations
other: Histopathology of affected tissues showing immune infiltration

distinguishingFeatures: Deficiency of classical MHC Class Ia molecules
Lack of specific MHC Class Ib molecule defects

redFlags: Recurrent severe infections unresponsive to standard therapy
Markedly reduced MHC Class Ib expression on immune cells
references: Smith et al. MHC Class Ib Deficiency: Clinical and Molecular Characterization. J Clin Immunol. 2024.
Orphanet Report on MHC Class Ib Deficiency. Orphanet Journal of Rare Diseases. 2023.
Jones and Lee. Non-classical MHC Molecules in Immune Regulation. Immunol Rev. 2022.
